items.title: 67848_Jimmy McPartland oral history interview
items.q: it was a more thrilling affair than Red Allen's at Cafe Society

ctx.x: ..... then he comes up and could not praise you any more than he does. And this is George Frazier and he says, 'the band that Jimmy McPartland had at Nicks was a quite magnificent little band indeed. And the news that it is there no longer can hardly be called glad tidings. Now I think that is a splendid beginning. (LAUGHTER).' It wasn't a flawless band and it's shortcomings were nothing if not palpable. But it's conception was absolutely perfect.

And in it's high, sensitive moments, it produced lovely unforgettable jazz." Jimmy this is really sincere and high praise. "For my money, it was a more thrilling affair than Red Allen's at Cafe Society and I say that in full realisation that Red's is one of the very best small bands ever.
"McPartland's was a rough band and at times an unforgivably sloppy one, but at its best on a good night when the guys were feeling right, it was practically unbeatable." (LAUGHTER).
